samples.question: The dark board is littered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly one cream CARD sits somewhere on it. Only what is drawn on the card decides the answer; every mark off the card is decoration and means nothing. The card carries six small square BEADS lying in two feed rows of three: an UPPER row and a LOWER row. The six beads all have different colours, one each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. Below the two rows lies the TRACK: six equally spaced square slots in a single horizontal line. Five slots are drawn as empty outlines and exactly one slot is filled solid dark - that filled slot is the MARKED slot. The beads are combed into the track by one vertical sweep line travelling across the card from left to right: the bead whose centre the sweep reaches first drops into the leftmost track slot, the bead reached next drops into the second slot, and so on, so the six beads fill the six slots from left to right in the order of their horizontal centres, no matter which feed row each bead came from. The two rows are staggered, so the sweep order alternates between the rows irregularly and cannot be read off either row on its own; a bead's own row never tells you its sweep position. The track slots are equally spaced, and a slot's position tells you nothing about the beads except its rank in the track. What colour is the bead that lands in the marked slot? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
